Purpose: To turn a secret reference into a value at the moment of use, and never earlier.
Caller and time: The harness layer before a call; the doctor for existence only.
Outputs: `handles`: yes or no. `exists`: `yes`, `no` or `unprobed`, and never the value. `resolve`: the
value, in memory, registered with the redactor. `boundHost`: the host the secret may be sent to.
Errors: `missing`; `inline-secret`, a configuration error; `unsafe-file`, for a target inside the
Guarantees of the core: A secret is resolved at the moment of use, passed by environment or standard input and never in an
argument list, written to no state, event, log or launch contract, and sent only to its bound
host. Every resolved value is registered with the redactor for exact-match removal.
Guarantees of an implementation: `exists` never prints or returns the value. A resolver makes no network call.
Failure of an implementation: A resolver that fails gives `missing`. For a role in use, that refuses the launch or, in a run,
Unknown-value rule: A reference with a scheme that no resolver handles is a configuration error. A value that is not
a reference where a reference is required is `inline-secret`.
Wave 1 implementations: `env:`, `file:`, `keychain:`. On Linux the existence check of the keychain reads `unprobed` until
a query is found that prints nothing.
